chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Back to Hamilton Lake in 1926 and the band fired over Carl's girlfriend
summary: He leads a band at the lake, but the religious pavilion owner fires them when he learns Carl is not married to the girl travelling with him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: When you did quit and went back to Defiance, Ohio, and you were formed a band and including some fellows from the old Chubb-Steinberg band---
Yes -- some of the guys around that didn't go on the road scene; they were replaced by other guys---
And, you went back to Hamilton Lake -- this was now 1926 --
Yeah.
---and you went back and you played at the same place you did before -- now, tell why the band
got fired---
Oh, yeah -- why the band got fired---
I think history would want to know.
Well, we went up thereand, of course---
Times have changed.
Times have changed since then. But, anyway, Carl had his girl with him and, uh, they were going to get married, of course, and they did.
Carl, being Carl Claus--(end of Side one of Tape 1).
Well, of course, the reason we got fired as I said -- they found out that Carl wasn't married and that was it (INAUDIBLE TAPE PORTION).
He and his girlfriend were living--- (AGAIN INAUDIBLE DEFECT IN TAPE)

Shortly after that, but this guy was a very religious man and I can understand that now -- why he did it. But, anyway, that was the last-- that was the last of Chub Steinberg thing because I went home again.
That was really your first real band that was played under your name though - wasn't it?
Yes.
Yeah - so that was the year of the "Wild Bill Davison" Band - that was the first--- only it wasn't "The Wild Bill" excuse me---
No, it was just Bill Davison---
No "Wild" yet.
